summary: Fix a real gap reported as 'why couldn't I drag a mymatasan node to a building or place?': in the fleet map's 'Not placed yet' tray, only unplaced cameras were draggable and the drop handler accepted only camera payloads, so an appliance row offered nothing but the no-fixed-location waiver toggle. Pinning an appliance's own marker on a plan is the only thing that ever writes ManagedNode.SiteId, so a tray that could say 'location not set' for a node's box but gave no way to fix it from there left the operator to hunt the node down in a place's editor palette instead. twin_tree.js now makes an appliance row draggable whenever its own box is unpinned and it isn't waived, carrying {nodeId, cameraId:'', name}; dropping it on a place or area opens that place's editor already holding it, exactly like a camera, and the click that follows pins the box (which records the node's site). The row also gained an explicit 'place' button beside the waiver toggle, mirroring the drag/button pairing camera rows already had, since the button is the only path that works without dragging. The drag payload's MIME was renamed text/tray-camera -> text/tray-pick because it can now carry either a camera or the appliance itself; 2 new i18n keys (tree.dragApplianceToPlace, tree.placeApplianceOnPlan) were added to all four dicts.
compatibility: Frontend-only UI fix; no new API routes, schema, or config. The backend write path is unchanged - ISiteService.AddPlacement/DeletePlacement was already the sole writer of SiteId; this only opens a second, faster UI path (drag) onto the same click-to-place flow the appliance already had via a place's editor palette. Existing installs need no migration. The MIME rename (text/tray-camera -> text/tray-pick) is an internal drag-and-drop payload type with no external consumers, so it carries no compatibility impact. Verified end to end on a throwaway sqlite install: dragging an appliance onto a place opened its editor pre-holding the node, and after clicking the plan the API reflected the new placement (empty cameraId) and the node's updated siteId/noFixedLocation. Build, go test, and npm run lint:undef clean; all four i18n dicts hold an identical key set.
